temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Small wings 400°F / 205°C · 18 min 425°F / 220°C · 23 min Standard flats and drumettes 400°F / 205°C · 22 min 425°F / 220°C · 28 min Large or jumbo wings 400°F / 205°C · 26 min 425°F / 220°C · 33 min Why air fryer wings come out soggy Wing skin is mostly water and fat. To crisp, the water has to evaporate and the fat has to render out, and both need a dry surface and space around each piece. Wings straight from the pack are wet, so the first several minutes go into steaming them; a crowded basket keeps that steam trapped, and the skin ends up leathery and pale however long it cooks. Sauce added before cooking makes it worse, because the sugar burns while the skin underneath stays soft. The fix is mostly preparation: dry the wings thoroughly, give them a single layer with gaps, and toss them in sauce only once they come out. Two uncrowded batches beat one crowded one. Worked example A pound of standard flats and drumettes, patted dry and tossed with salt and a teaspoon of baking powder. Preheat 4 minutes, cook at 400°F for 22 minutes and shake or turn them at 11 minutes. Jumbo wings need about 26 minutes. Toss in sauce straight out of the basket. The oven version of the same tray is 425°F for around 28 minutes, with much less crunch. How to tell they are done Wings are safe at 165°F (74°C), but they are better well past that: dark meat and the connective tissue around the joint soften at 175–190°F, which is why a properly crispy wing is never undercooked. Look for skin that is deep golden, tight and blistered, and meat that pulls away from the bone at the joint. If the skin is still pale and soft at the end of the time, give them three more minutes rather than raising the temperature. Before they go in Dry the wings with paper towel, or leave them uncovered on a rack in the fridge for a few hours. A light dusting of baking powder (not soda) raises the pH of the skin and helps it blister. Salt them, but skip oil: wings carry enough fat of their own. Separate wings that have been sold joined at the tip, and arrange the pieces skin side up without overlapping. Related presets Chicken breast 375°F · 16 min · flip at 8 Chicken thighs 380°F · 24 min · flip at 12 Chicken drumsticks 380°F · 22 min · flip at 11 425°F oven to air fryer, every food → Oven to air fryer converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How long do chicken wings take in the air fryer? About 22 minutes at 400°F for standard fresh wings, shaken or turned at 11 minutes. Small wings take around 18 minutes, jumbo wings around 26. What temperature are chicken wings done at? They are safe at 165°F (74°C), but most cooks take wings higher, to 175–190°F, for tender meat and crisp skin. Should I sauce wings before or after air frying? After. Sauce on raw wings burns before the skin crisps underneath. Toss the cooked wings in warm sauce in a bowl and serve straight away. Why use baking powder on air fryer wings? A light coat of baking powder makes the skin more alkaline, which helps it brown and blister. Use about a teaspoon per pound, and make sure it is baking powder, not baking soda. Can I cook frozen wings with this setting? No. Frozen wings need their own time; use frozen mode, which keeps the heat high and adds shakes to separate pieces that froze together.
